nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $x$ a variable and $b$ a Boolean value. If a clause $D$ is derivable by resolution from the restriction of $\varphi$ by the literal $(x, b)$, then some clause $D_0$ is derivable by resolution from $\varphi$ such that every literal of $D_0$ is either a literal of $D$ or the complementary literal $(x, \lnot b)$.
nodes.title: Lifting lemma

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $\ell$ a literal. A clause $C$ belongs to the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ if and only if there is a clause $C_0$ of $\varphi$ that does not contain $\ell$ such that $C$ is the restriction of $C_0$ by $\ell$.
nodes.title: Clauses of a restricted formula

nodes.summary: If a CNF formula $\varphi$ has no variables and is not satisfiable, then the empty clause is one of the clauses of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Unsatisfiable formulas without variables contain the empty clause

nodes.summary: If the empty clause is derivable by resolution from a CNF formula $\varphi$, then $\varphi$ is not satisfiable.
nodes.title: Refutable formulas are unsatisfiable

nodes.summary: A CNF formula has a resolution refutation iff it is unsatisfiable.
nodes.title: Soundness and refutation completeness

nodes.summary: Refutation completeness of resolution: every unsatisfiable CNF formula has a resolution derivation of the empty clause.
nodes.title: Refutation completeness

nodes.summary: Given a CNF formula $\varphi$, the clauses derivable from $\varphi$ by resolution form the smallest set $S$ of clauses that contains every clause of $\varphi$ and, for every variable $x$ and all clauses $C, D \in S$ such that $C$ contains the literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ and $D$ contains the literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$, contains the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Resolution derivability

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $C$, $D$ clauses. The resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$ is the clause consisting of the literals of $C$ other than $(x, \mathrm{true})$, in order, followed by the literals of $D$ other than $(x, \mathrm{false})$, in order.
nodes.title: Resolvent of two clauses

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $C$, $D$ clauses. Every assignment that satisfies both $C$ and $D$ satisfies the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Resolution rule soundness

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula. Every clause derivable by resolution from $\varphi$ is satisfied by every assignment that satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Soundness of resolution

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
